title: let, var, type inference, and strong typing that shows up early

videos.script: Every lesson in this course asks you to type a program and read what comes back. So this one starts by giving you somewhere to type. {{lab}} One Ubuntu machine, your own or a virtual one. A list of libraries from Ubuntu's archive, and one archive from swift.org. Its signature checked, and the compiler asked what version it is. {{fails}} Then three ways that goes wrong, each made on purpose, each with a message that names its own cause. {{hello}} Then the first program. Four lines, run straight from the source, and then compiled to a file you can run on its own. {{let}} Then the first thing Swift asks of you. Two words for a name. Let, which never changes, and var, which can. The compiler holds you to the first, and nudges you towards it. {{types}} And types. You will not write many, and every name still has one. You will see the compiler refuse to add a whole number to a decimal without being told how. And you will see a program stop rather than get a sum wrong. By the end you have a working machine, and a small program about one week of study.
